pr.body: Interpolating queries as the initial step. Fixes #107530
pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: The target is interpolated here and is then passed to `datasource.runQuery`, whose inherited backend-query path applies `applyTemplateVariables` again. The second pass expands tokens introduced by the first pass, so the backend receives a different query from the user's selected literal value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Template replacement becomes non-idempotent: variable-like text produced by a variable expansion is treated as a new variable on the subsequent backend execution pass.
raw_findings.impact: The target is interpolated here and is then passed to `datasource.runQuery`, whose inherited backend-query path applies `applyTemplateVariables` again. The second pass expands tokens introduced by the first pass, so the backend receives a different query from the user's selected literal value.
raw_findings.root_cause: Pre-interpolated targets retain the original scoped variables when they are handed to `runQuery`, causing the backend datasource interpolation hook to process them a second time.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Ensure split subrequests are not interpolated again by the backend path after this preprocessing step, for example by constructing the grouped execution requests with already-consumed custom scoped variables (while retaining any required backend built-ins), or by adding an explicit already-interpolated execution path.
raw_findings.title: Avoid applying template variables twice for split requests
raw_findings.trigger: With Loki query splitting enabled, run a query containing a custom variable whose selected literal value itself contains another variable token (for example, `$outer` resolves to the literal `$inner` while `inner` is also defined).

raw_findings.body: `applyTemplateVariables` adds the ad-hoc filters here, and `runQuery` applies the same backend interpolation hook again with the unchanged `request.filters`. Each split request therefore contains duplicate copies of every ad-hoc label matcher, unnecessarily inflating and parsing the generated LogQL; shard splitting adds another pre-execution application on top of this path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The same ad-hoc filter set is appended repeatedly to the selector sent for each split request.
raw_findings.impact: `applyTemplateVariables` adds the ad-hoc filters here, and `runQuery` applies the same backend interpolation hook again with the unchanged `request.filters`. Each split request therefore contains duplicate copies of every ad-hoc label matcher, unnecessarily inflating and parsing the generated LogQL; shard splitting adds another pre-execution application on top of this path.
raw_findings.root_cause: The preprocessed queries and the original filter-bearing request are both passed into the normal backend query execution path, which independently applies ad-hoc filters.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After applying filters during split-query preprocessing, prevent the execution request from carrying those filters into the backend interpolation hook (or centralize interpolation so it occurs exactly once per subrequest).
raw_findings.title: Do not add ad-hoc filters twice to time-split queries
raw_findings.trigger: With time-based Loki query splitting enabled, execute a request that has one or more `request.filters` ad-hoc filters.

finding.title: Avoid applying template variables twice for split requests
finding.trigger: With Loki query splitting enabled, run a query containing a custom variable whose selected literal value itself contains another variable token (for example, `$outer` resolves to the literal `$inner` while `inner` is also defined).
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that runQuery applies applyTemplateVariables again is not supported by the code. Looking at datasource.ts L350-357, runQuery() calls super.query() which goes to DataSourceWithBackend. The applyTemplateVariables method is called by DataSourceWithBackend only when filterQuery returns true, but the queries passed to runSplitGroupedQueries already have targets set from the pre-interpolated queries array. The candidate assumes double interpolation occurs but does not prove the backend path re-applies template variables to already-interpolated queries.

finding.title: Do not add ad-hoc filters twice to time-split queries
finding.trigger: With time-based Loki query splitting enabled, execute a request that has one or more `request.filters` ad-hoc filters.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that ad-hoc filters are added twice is unsubstantiated. The applyTemplateVariables at line 299 adds filters, but the subsequent runQuery path in runSplitGroupedQueries (line 180) passes the subRequest with already-interpolated targets. The candidate assumes DataSourceWithBackend.query() re-applies filters, but there is no evidence in the provided context that the backend interpolation hook processes request.filters again on queries that were already processed by applyTemplateVariables.
